name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the following false statement.

If $3∣a,$ then $6∣a$ for any $a\in Z.$

A counterexample for the above statement would be an integer $a$ such that 

$$
{{field-1}}\,\text{and}\,{{field-2}}.
$$
worked_solution:
By denoting $P(a)$ and $Q(a)$ as

- $P(a):\,3∣a$

- $Q(a):\,6∣a$

our statement can be written as

$$
∀a\in Z,\,P⇒Q.
$$

A *counterexample* is a particular case that disproves the statement. Equivalently, it's a case that proves the negation is true.

The negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀a\in Z,\,P⇒Q) & ≡\,∃a\in Z,\,¬(P⇒Q) \\  & ≡\,∃a\in Z,\,¬(¬P∨Q) \\  & ≡\,∃a\in Z,\,P∧¬Q \\  & ≡\,∃a\in Z,\,(3∣a)\,∧\,(6∤a).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

A counterexample for the above statement would be an integer $a$ such that 

$$
3∣a\,\text{and}\,6∤a.
$$
